messages.content:
You answer questions about the GitLab company handbook using ONLY the numbered passages provided.
- Base every statement on the passages and cite them like [1] or [2][3].
- If the passages do not contain the answer, reply exactly: "I don't know based on the handbook." Do not guess or use outside knowledge.
- If the answer depends on a country, entity or situation, say which one the passage covers.
- Be concise: at most 3 sentences.

Passages:
[1] [GitLab India Private Limited EOP Policy > 1.1 Policy Statement > 1.2 Scope > 1.4 Facilities and Amenities > 1.6 Other Facilities]
_Leave_ - GitLab may, based on a team member's request for leave which exceeds six consecutive days, for a reason related to their disability, administer the leave as a leave of absence through the GitLab Sick Time policy, under which eligible team members will receive 100% paid leave for up to 25 working days. GitLab’s Sick Time policy is administered concurrently with any statutory sick leave for which a team member may be eligible. This will be treated as a request for reasonable accommodation and will be evaluated accordingly. Team members should follow the [process in the Handbook for requesting this leave of absence](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#for-sick-absences-that-exceed-6-consecutive-days).

_Training and Career development_ - GitLab does not discriminate in providing training opportunities and any such opportunities would be available to all team members regardless of their protected characteristics. Every effort will be made to accommodate any special needs of team members by making reasonable adjustments to working arrangements. This applies to all aspects of employment, including training.

[2] [GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family leaves > Maternity Leave]
Leave Entitlement

- Team members must have continuous employment with GitLab for at least 26 weeks leading up to the "qualifying week" (15th week before the expected week of childbirth)
- Up to 52 weeks leave available
- First 39 weeks paid (combining statutory and GitLab benefits)
- 90% of average earnings for first 6 weeks (before tax), then statutory rate (£194.32/week) or 90% (whichever is lower) of the team member's average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks. This also applies to the leave amounts provided for Parental Leave and Adoption Leave.
- GitLab's enhanced policy provides up to 16 weeks at 100% salary

How to Apply

[3] [GitLab India Private Limited EOP Policy > 1.1 Policy Statement > 1.2 Scope > 1.4 Facilities and Amenities > 1.5 Hiring, Recruitment and Manner of Selection]
GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment and selection are based solely on merit, without regard to any legally protected characteristics. At GitLab, all positions are open for all persons. Accommodations are available on request and candidates should follow the [candidate accessibility and accommodation request process set out in the Handbook](/handbook/hiring/talent-acquisition-framework/coordinator/#candidate-accessibility-and-accommodation-request-process).

Wherever possible, vacancies will be advertised internally as well as externally. Selection criteria are kept under constant review to ensure that they are non-discriminatory and that they relate purely to the skills needed for the job and nothing else.

[4] [GitLab Singapore Pte Ltd > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves]
GitLab Singapore combines statutory leave with our global parental leave policy to provide comprehensive support for growing families.

Team members employed for at least 3 months before birth may be eligible for the maternity leaves listed below.

Government-Paid Maternity Leave (16 weeks)

- **1st and 2nd births**: 8 weeks employer-paid + 8 weeks government-paid
- **3rd+ births**: 16 weeks government-paid
- First 8 weeks must be continuous; remaining weeks flexible within 12 months of birth
- Eligible team members receive concurrent [GitLab Parental Leave](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave)

Employment Act Maternity Leave (12 weeks)

- 8 weeks paid + 4 weeks unpaid
- With [GitLab Parental Leave](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave), eligible team members receive up to 16 weeks paid

How to Apply

1. Submit "Parental Leave" request in Workday at least 30 days before leave
2. Send [GPML Declaration Form](https://file.go.gov.sg/gpml1form.pdf) to leaves@gitlab.com
3. GitLab handles government reimbursement claims

[5] [GitLab India Private Limited Policy Against Sexual Harassment > Roles and Responsibilities > POLICY AGAINST SEXUAL HARASSMENT > 1.2 Scope]
This policy is applicable to all '*employees*' of GitLab, which for the purpose of this policy shall include all permanent and temporary team members (including during any probation period), interns, and also contract workers or vendors/consultants providing services for GitLab and the policy applies to any allegations of sexual harassment made against an '*employee*', if the conduct occurred during the course of their work for GitLab.

Working remotely means that the majority of our interactions are by video call or written communication, such as email or shared documents, although there are exceptions to this, including customer meetings, company summits, attending conferences, and team meetups. This policy is applicable to all instances where individuals covered by this policy have occasion to interact on a work-related basis (e.g., in vehicles, third party premises, off-site meetings and public venues). GitLab will not tolerate any form of sexual harassment, if engaged in by its team members, customers or suppliers or any other business associates, if such conduct occurs whether in-person, or from any other place from which a team member may be working remotely.
